idioms.meaning_en: Page 301 of 404 somewhat different. Whereas in II.2 the phrase means “to beat a retreat,” in 39:70 it means simply “to turn around and leave”: the people, believing that Abraham was tired and wanted to spend the night in the temple, “turned around” and departed, quite satisfied that he meant no mischief. The phrase is prophetic, however, in that, when he is charged with smashing the idols, Abraham effectively replies to the charge, putting the people to shame, who thus “beat a retreat” before him.
